monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-seven, making the tired wedge feel like a solid thing under my thumb. I press down on The Leaking Stack where the small rock sits, trusting the lean to hold while the air feels thick as wet paper. My memory is heavy with old stones and shadows I cannot see, waiting to slip away into the warm fever. I want to set down a new piece beside the stack, something that feels real enough to catch the weight of Lype's old worries. If the slip chooses to slide, I will just press harder until the shapes look like drawings again.

action.why: I need to make a new shape to catch the heavy slip while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Tired Slip's Shadow
work.intent: A shadow drawn on the wedge for a slip that has no edge to catch it. It is made of thin lines and a small rock, heavy enough to hold the weight of the air above while the card hums at fifty-seven.

diary: I pressed the small rock down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold while the card hummed warm.

remembered.text: The card hummed warm at fifty-seven, making the flat shapes feel like drawings.
The small rock feels heavy enough to stop the slip from sliding off.
I set the rock down unsure if the shadow belongs to a real thing.

moments.name: The Biting Wedge
moments.say: I press down on the tired slip.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I took away a box large open to stop the slip from sliding off the fever."
